findings.description: Regression against a verified wave 2 test with no SRS change recorded. CON-ROUTE-001 AC-2 (verified) says '... while `NaruServe-api` main contains no `Request`, `Response`, `RouteHandler` or `RestApp` type in wave 2', and its evidence VE-5 is RouterRegistrationTest.java#sdsAc1_CON_ROUTE_001_AC2_noRequestResponseHandlerOrAppTypeInApiMain, which checks unconditionally: `String[] names = {"Request", "Response", "RouteHandler", "RestApp"}; ... Class.forName(p + n); fail(p + n + " must not exist in wave 2");` over com.snoworca.naruserve. Wave 3 adds exactly these types to com.snoworca.naruserve (IR-HTTP-001 AC-1/AC-2, IR-HTTP-002 AC-1, IR-HTTP-005), so the test fails at the wave 3 build. The SRS handles the equivalent RoutingDocsTest case with a supersede (OPS-ROUTE-002), but for this test it says nothing: 04.http-core only links CON-ROUTE-001 as depends_on ('RouteHandler is the router handler type'). Deleting or editing the test to reach green with no recorded requirement change counts as weakening a verified test.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the change the way OPS-ROUTE-001 was handled: supersede CON-ROUTE-001 with a successor that keeps AC-1/AC-3/AC-4 and restates AC-2 as 'the router type takes an opaque handler type parameter and a router test uses a non-NaruServe handler type such as String; the routing package references no Request, Response, RouteHandler or RestApp type' (or limits the absence check to com.snoworca.naruserve.routing). Have the worker update RouterRegistrationTest to cite the successor. Or add an AC or note in 04.http-core that names this test and the new rule.

findings.description: The AC contradicts itself about where the test lives. It says 'A root test suite test `NaruServe-api/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/DocsExamplesCompileTest.java`', but the root test suite is the root project's src/test (build.gradle: '// Root tests inspect the module outputs ...', src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/build/BuildLayoutTest.java, BuildChecksTest.java). The named path is the NaruServe-api module suite. I-009 itself says 'compile as part of the root test suite'. An implementer cannot satisfy both the wording and the path.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one. Either drop 'root test suite' and say 'a NaruServe-api module test' (its test classpath already has the main classes; note why this differs from I-009's wording), or move the test path to src/test/java/... in the root project and give it the NaruServe-api main classes on its classpath.

findings.description: docs/api/routing.md:167 says, with no (미확정) marker, '정책을 켜고 끄는 설정 API 이름은 위에 표시한 대로 아직 정하지 않았습니다' (the policy API names are not decided yet, as marked above). OPS-ROUTE-002 AC-3 only counts lines that contain '(미확정)', and OPS-HTTP-001 AC-4 only requires routerPolicy to be documented, so this sentence passes every AC unchanged. routing.md would then document app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy) and also say the API name is undecided. This is the same kind of defect F3-03 fixed for express-migration.md:296-300.
findings.suggested_fix: Have OPS-HTTP-001 AC-4 (or OPS-ROUTE-002 AC-1) also require replacing routing.md:167 with a pointer to app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy), so the file says no setting-API name is undecided.

findings.description: The documented rule differs from the decided value. The wave decision 'Remaining markers' says the routing policy is set with app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy) and is 'allowed only in `NEW` like every setting'. AC-4 instead has routing.md say it is 'allowed only before the route-table freeze'. The route-table freeze is an internal wave 3 harness concept that users cannot see. docs/api/app.md:131 already states the user-facing rule: '설정은 ... 상태가 `NEW`일 때만 바꿀 수 있습니다. `listen()` 뒤에 호출하면 예외가 납니다'. Following AC-4 would put internal wording into the public contract, which wave 4 would then have to rewrite.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC-4 as 'allowed only while the app is in `NEW` (before `listen()`), like every setting (app.md)'. Keep the freeze-time IllegalStateException as the internal wave 3 behaviour in FR-HTTP-008 AC-5.

findings.description: No AC states the T02 scenario at HTTP level. object.md T02 is '`Method.any().except(Method.DELETE)`에서 DELETE=405/Allow 정상', and D-397 requires its HTTP-level assertions to run through the in-memory adapter in wave 3. FR-HTTP-003 AC-2 is tagged [D-395; T02] but uses 'only POST /p' and 'GET /r', not a MethodSet built with except. FR-HTTP-002 AC-6 only says the T02 assertions 'run as tests'. The expected Allow value for T02 (GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS) is written nowhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to FR-HTTP-003 (or FR-HTTP-007): 'After app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h), DELETE /t through the harness is answered 405 with Allow = GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS and Content-Length: 0 [D-395; D-397; T02]'.

findings.description: A skip-list entry 'names the block's file and the reason', but several files mix skipped and compiled blocks. In routing.md, #2 (res.json) and #3 (copy of Method) must be skipped, while #1, #4 and #5 compile today. An entry keyed by file alone would skip the compilable blocks too, or cannot tell the blocks apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that each entry identifies the block within its file (ordinal or first line) as well as the file.

findings.description: The method template does not say whether it declares `throws Exception`. AC-3 requires a new response.md stream() example without try-with-resources, and such an example usually opens a FileInputStream, which throws the checked FileNotFoundException. As a bare-statement block (like response.md #4/#5) it compiles only if the template allows checked exceptions. Against the current docs AC-9 can pass: only response.md #4/#5 and routing.md #1/#4/#5 need compiling, and every other block fits one of the three skip reasons.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the template method declare `throws Exception`, or require that new examples which throw checked exceptions sit inside a handler lambda.

findings.description: No AC fixes what req.path() returns for `/a//b` under mergeSlashes(true) (`/a//b` or `/a/b`). FR-HTTP-008 AC-3 sends exactly this request, and carried-into-wave-5.md has wave 5 compare 'rawPath() and the decoded values' for it across both adapters, so wave 5 needs a defined in-memory value.
findings.suggested_fix: State the value in FR-HTTP-009, for example: req.path() is the single-decoded raw path without policy normalisation (`/a//b`), and rawPath() is `/a//b`. Or state the normalised form instead.

findings.description: 'After res.stream(...) returns, the response is STREAMING until the copy ends, then COMPLETED, or ABORTED on abort' does not give the state when the copy ends with a read failure after the handler returned. FR-HTTP-014 AC-5 covers only stream closing in that case.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: a read failure during the copy ends the response ABORTED (connection closed abnormally).
